title: Disruption of the Blood-Spinal Cord Barrier Using Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in a Rat Model
protocol: Acquire a focused ultrasound transducer system suitable for BSCB opening in rats.
Affix the 3D-printed probe holder and water cone on the transducer.
Ensure a watertight seal between the cone and transducer.
Sterilize a 50 µm thick, acoustically transparent polyester membrane.
Affix the sterilized membrane to the bottom of the water cone using a rubber band.
Fill the water cone with degassed and deionized water using the inlet tube.
Guide air bubbles to the outlet valve while filling the cone with water through the inlet valve.
Close all valves and rotate the cone until one large bubble remains, then guide this bubble to the outlet valve.
Connect the wave generator and RF drive amplifier to the transducer via the matching network cables.
Attach the probe holder to the stereotactic arm.
Affix the stereotactic arm to the fixation plate assembly.
Anesthetize the rat with a mixture of isoflurane and medical air in an induction chamber attached to a charcoal filter canister.
Set the gas flow rate to 400 mL/min and the isoflurane vaporizer between 1.5%-2.5% for anesthesia induction.
Record the weight of the sedated rat.
Perform a toe pinch test.
Place the rat back inside the induction chamber for an additional 1 min if jerking or movement is observed in response to the pinch.
Repeat the toe pinch test until the rat is fully anesthetized and remains so.
Place a heating pad on the fixation plate.
Place a sterile absorbent pad on the fixation plate.
Position the rat on the absorbent pad.
Apply eye ointment.
Place a rectal thermometer to monitor body temperature.
Palpate the last rib of the rat at the T13 vertebra.
Shave the fur off the dorsal surface between the last rib and neck using an electric razor.
Wipe the exposed skin with gauze dipped in 10% iodopovidone.
Create a midline incision using iris scissors.
Dissect through the fascia until the spinous processes and lamina are exposed.
Remove bone with offset bone nippers and angled blade iris scissors to expose the spinal cord.
Perform a three-level laminectomy using a 3 cm incision.
Secure the rat to the fixation plate by clamping the spinous processes adjacent to the laminectomy.
Pull the spine taut slightly before locking the clamps to minimize curvature.
Adjust the position of the transducer with the stereotactic arm until it is located exactly above the laminectomy.
Affix the laser apparatus to the bottom of the water cone.
Lower the laser apparatus until the laser point is visible.
Adjust the lateral position of the transducer until the laser point is above the target location for BSCB disruption.
Remove the laser apparatus from the setup.
Fill the space between the cone and spinal cord with degassed ultrasound gel.
Ensure that no air bubbles are present in the ultrasound gel for maximal coupling.
Set the parameters for sonication on the TPO.
Choose a frequency close to 250 kHz for maximal power.
Set the focus distance at 40 mm.
Use a range of pressures between 0.2-2.1 MPa.
Select burst lengths between 10-25 ms.
Sonicate for times ranging from 2-5 minutes.
Prepare a microbubble solution according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Avoid introducing air into the microbubble solution.
Shake the vial and syringe regularly to prevent uneven dispersion of MBs.
Check the manufacturer's guide for the expiration time of the microbubbles.
Insert a 22 G tail vein catheter.
Flush the catheter with 0.2 mL of heparinized saline (500 IU/mL).
Dip the rat's tail in warm water and place a tourniquet at the base to enlarge the vein diameter.
Inject 1 mL/kg of 3% EBD into the catheter via the tail vein catheter.
Flush the catheter with 0.2 mL of heparinized saline after injecting EBD.
Check for blue color change in the dorsal spinal vein and extremities of the rat to confirm successful catheterization.
Inject a 0.2 mL bolus of MBs into the catheter.
Flush the catheter with 0.2 mL of heparinized saline.
Start sonication 1-2 min after injection of MBs.
Transcardially perfuse the rat with 100 mL of cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) until blood runs clear.
Transcardially perfuse with 100 mL of cold 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Remove the spinal cord and place it in 4% PFA at 4°C overnight.
Replace the PFA with PBS the following day.
Isolate a 2 cm section surrounding the location of sonication using a razor blade.
Split the section down the midline with the blade.
Section the split section into 10 µm thick sections using a microtome.
Stain with hematoxylin for 3 min and eosin for 1 min for bright-field visualization.
Deparaffinize the slides containing the spinal cord sections.
Counterstain with 25 µL of 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) dissolved in the mounting medium (0.5 µg/mL).
Incubate at 4°C for at least 10 min.
Avoid light to prevent bleaching.
Use a fluorescent microscope to image all the slides.
Set excitation at 470 nm for EBD autofluorescence.
Set emission at 540 nm for EBD autofluorescence.
Observe EBD autofluorescence in the red channel.
Observe DAPI fluorescence in the blue channel.
Use a light microscope to image the H&E slides.
Disinfect the skin with iodopovidone before incision.
Administer buprenorphine subcutaneously (0.05 mg/kg) before surgery for survival techniques.
Continue providing subcutaneous buprenorphine every 12 hours at least 3 days post-operatively.
House rats with nutritionally fortified water gel if urinary retention or abnormal gait occurs.
Manually express bladders twice per day until reflex voiding is recovered.
Euthanize the rat if there is complete paralysis of hind limbs or intractable pain.
